# Diagramwise

> Diagramwise is a system design practice tool. You build architectures on a visual canvas, explain your assumptions and trade-offs, and get structured feedback on scalability, reliability, and data design.

Diagramwise is a product of Next Zen (https://next-zen.dev/), which also builds Learn Algo and Orchestrator.

## Features

- **Architecture simulator:** In Design Studio, select Simulate to run live traffic through a design. Set load up to 100,000 requests per second, choose a steady, ramp-up, burst or daily-cycle pattern, adjust playback speed, and watch each component's throughput, busy level and failures. Slow a component down or make it return errors to see where the design breaks, and compare runs.
- **MCP server:** Diagramwise has a remote MCP (Model Context Protocol) server at https://mcp.diagramwise.com/mcp. Connect it as a custom connector in ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini Apps, sign in with a Diagramwise account, and the assistant can create and save architectures to that account. Setup steps are in the "AI connections" dialog on https://diagramwise.com/.

## Key pages

- [Practice problems](https://diagramwise.com/problems/): System design, infrastructure, AI/ML and MLOps architecture problems with requirements and scale assumptions.
- [Learning paths](https://diagramwise.com/learning-paths/): Structured modules covering system design foundations such as caching, database scaling and replication.
- [System design interview guide](https://diagramwise.com/system-design-interview/): A repeatable method for turning ambiguous prompts into requirements, estimates and architecture decisions.
- [System design practice](https://diagramwise.com/system-design-practice/): How to practice system design effectively.
- [AI system design interview](https://diagramwise.com/ai-system-design-interview/): AI and ML system design across data pipelines, retrieval, inference and evaluation.
- [Kubernetes architecture](https://diagramwise.com/kubernetes-architecture/): Kubernetes architecture design practice.
